children: For the past year, Canada's public sector has been a weak spot in the country's labor market, Statistics Canada data show. This coincides with the arrival of Canada PM Mark Carney, whose government has pledged to curtail operating expenditures through, among other things, a 10% cut to federal payrolls. Employment across Canada's public sector fell 20,000 in August, and is down 0.4% on a 12-month basis. Conversely, private-sector employment rose 1.1% in August from a year ago. Broken down further, the public-administration category has recorded job losses of roughly 19,000, 21,200 and 13,500 on a 3-, 6- and 12-month basis, respectively. Meanwhile, trade-exposed manufacturing sector recorded jobs gains over those time periods. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)
